Usage Description (What does it do): LiFePO4 lithium iron phosphate 12.8V 1100mAh rechargeable battery pack. Primary power source for all VEX V5 robots. Connects directly to the V5 Brain via a proprietary slide-lock connector. Outputs up to 20A continuous enough for 10 motors at peak. Built-in battery management system tracks charge via coulomb counting. Provides 30 or more minutes of heavy driving per charge and recharges in under 60 minutes. Also called V5 battery or robot battery.
Appearance Description: Large thick black rectangular plastic housing. LED charge indicator strip on one face. Heavier and denser than most VEX components. Slide-lock connector port on one short end. Roughly the size of a large smartphone but much thicker. Solid black with no moving parts visible.

Usage Description (What does it do): Three-wire digital contact sensor that returns a binary high or low signal when its lever arm is pressed or released. Used to detect end stops hard motion limits object presence or button presses. Common at the end of linear slides or arms to prevent overtravel. Also called micro switch or snap-action switch.
Appearance Description: Small white plastic rectangular body approximately 1 inch long with a protruding metal lever arm actuator on one end. Lever arm is silver metal and swings down when pressed. Red actuator button visible near lever hinge. White and red 3-wire cable with white 3-pin rectangular connector.

Usage Description (What does it do): Plastic clip-style brackets that secure the VEX V5 Robot Battery to the robot frame. Clip directly onto the battery body and attach to VEX structural metal using standard screws through mounting flanges. Prevents battery shifting during robot movement. Used in pairs with two mounts per battery.
Appearance Description: Black plastic curved clip brackets. Profile matches the edge of the V5 battery. Flat flanged tabs on each side with screw holes for structural attachment. Lightweight and compact.

Usage Description (What does it do): Large high-strength nylon cable ties used to secure heavy components such as the battery pneumatic tubing or thick cable bundles to the robot frame. Single-use fastener that must be cut to remove. Much stronger and wider strap than standard zip ties. Also called large cable ties or heavy duty cable ties.
Appearance Description: Black nylon plastic. Wide flat strap noticeably wider than standard zip ties. Self-locking ratchet head at one end. Longer overall length than standard zip ties. Smooth on one face and toothed rack on the other for locking mechanism.

Usage Description (What does it do): Passive extension cable that lengthens the cable reach of any 3-wire VEX sensor or actuator. Plugs inline between the sensor and the 3-wire port on the V5 Brain or Cortex. Carries both power and signal. Can be chained. Also called sensor extension cable or 3-wire extender.
Appearance Description: White and red parallel or twisted wire with black plastic 3-pin rectangular connectors on each end. One male and one female connector for inline daisy-chaining. Wire has distinct white and red coloring with black connector ends.

Usage Description (What does it do): Three-wire digital contact sensor with a broad button face designed to detect bumps or collisions with walls or game objects. Returns a digital high or low signal when pressed. Often mounted at the front of a robot for collision detection or as a large-area limit switch. Also called contact sensor or collision sensor.
Appearance Description: Grey rectangular plastic body with a large flat circular grey button covering most of the front face. Wider and flatter face than the limit switch. 3-wire cable with white 3-pin rectangular connector exits from the body.

Usage Description (What does it do): Three-wire analog rotation sensor that returns a voltage proportional to the absolute angular position of an axle inserted into its center. Unlike the shaft encoder it gives absolute position not relative counts. Range is approximately 0 to 265 degrees. Useful for tracking arm angle or mechanism position. Also called rotary potentiometer rotary position sensor or analog angle sensor.
Appearance Description: Red plastic square housing with a circular center hole for axle insertion. Slightly larger than a shaft collar. 3-wire cable exits the body. Distinctive red color distinguishes it from other sensors.

Usage Description (What does it do): Proprietary bidirectional communication cable connecting VEX V5 components including motors sensors vision sensor and radio to the V5 Brain smart ports. Carries both power and digital CAN-bus-style communication in a single cable. Required for all V5 motors and V5-generation sensors. The V5 Brain has 21 smart ports. Also called V5 smart cable V5 port cable or VEX smart wire.
Appearance Description: Flat black ribbon-style cable. Clear or translucent square RJ-style plastic connectors on each end with a small locking tab. Thinner and flatter than traditional round cables. Both connectors are identical.

Usage Description (What does it do): Automotive-style blade fuses that protect VEX robot circuits from overcurrent damage. Internal metal strip melts and permanently breaks the circuit when current exceeds the rated limit. Single-use and non-resettable and must be replaced after blowing. Used in VEX Cortex-based power distribution systems. Also called blade fuses or automotive fuses.
Appearance Description: Small rectangular plastic housing with two flat metal blade pins protruding from the bottom. Transparent or translucent plastic body allows visual inspection of the internal metal bridge to see if it is blown. Typically red but may be other colors. Very small component.

Usage Description (What does it do): Primary actuator for VEX V5 robots. Available in 11W high-power and 5.5W variants. Uses swappable internal gear cartridges for three speed-torque ratios: 36:1 at 100 RPM high torque or 18:1 at 200 RPM balanced or 6:1 at 600 RPM high speed. Built-in quadrature encoder provides position velocity and direction feedback to the Brain. Connects to Brain via Smart Cable. Accepts both 1/8 inch standard and 1/4 inch high-strength axles. Also called V5 motor smart motor or VEX motor.
Appearance Description: Square black plastic housing with three side-mounted attachment flanges with screw holes. Single red LED on the smart port side indicates status. Clear window on one face reveals the color of the swappable gear cartridge inside. Red cartridge means 100 RPM green means 200 RPM blue means 600 RPM. Output shaft protrudes from one end. Compact dense cube-like shape.

Usage Description (What does it do): Electronic speed controller that interfaces the VEX 2-Wire Motor 393 with VEX Cortex or V5 Brain 3-wire ports. Converts the PWM signal from the controller into a variable voltage that drives the 393 motor. Required adapter between any 3-wire port and the 2-wire 393 motor. Also called MC29 or motor controller.
Appearance Description: Small black rectangular module slightly larger than a matchbook. A 3-wire cable exits one end for connection to the controller port. A 2-wire cable exits the opposite end for connection to the 393 motor. Black plastic housing with wires on both opposing sides.

Usage Description (What does it do): Primary motor in the VEX EDR Cortex system providing 60 percent more output power than the older VEX 269 motor. Must be used with a Motor Controller 29 when connected to 3-wire ports. Can accept an integrated optical encoder module add-on. Used in drive trains arms and all actuated mechanisms in VEX EDR competition robots. Also called 393 motor two-wire motor or VEX EDR motor.
Appearance Description: Medium-sized motor with a black plastic body and a distinctive green plastic end cap on the motor end. Two short wire leads with a 2-pin connector exit from the side. Metal output shaft protrudes from the front face. Noticeably heavier and larger than the V5 Smart Motor.

Usage Description (What does it do): Three-wire optical quadrature shaft encoder that mounts around a rotating axle to measure direction of rotation rotational speed and total accumulated rotation in ticks at 360 ticks per revolution. Used to track wheel travel distance arm angle or flywheel RPM. Requires an axle to pass through its center. Also called optical shaft encoder quadrature encoder or rotation sensor.
Appearance Description: Two-part clamshell design that clips around an axle. Upper half is a square red plastic housing. Lower half is a larger gray rectangular base. The red half snaps closed onto the gray half around the inserted axle. 3-wire cable exits from the housing.

Usage Description (What does it do): Standard-size nylon cable ties used throughout VEX robots to bundle wires secure sensors fasten tubing or loosely attach lightweight components. Single-use fastener cut to remove. Essential consumable hardware in all VEX builds. Also called cable ties or wire ties.
Appearance Description: Black nylon plastic. Thin narrow strap significantly thinner and shorter than heavy duty zip ties. Self-locking ratchet head at one end. Smooth on one face and toothed rack on the other.

Location: Metal Room, Bottom Shelf 1, Row 2, Section 2
Usage Description (What does it do): The largest size of VEX wheel providing maximum ground contact area traction and top speed at a given motor RPM. Mounts on standard 1/8 inch or 1/4 inch high-strength axles using wheel inserts. Used as primary drive wheels on competition robots when maximum speed or traction is needed. Also called large traction wheels or big wheels.
Appearance Description: Large diameter circular wheel with a green plastic spoked hub and rubber or foam tread ring on the outer circumference. Significantly larger in diameter than medium or small VEX wheels. Green spokes radiate from the center hub to the outer rim.

Location: Metal Room, Bottom Shelf 1, Row 2, Section 3
Usage Description (What does it do): VEX claw mechanism functioning as an end-effector on robot arms. Driven by a motor and axle to open and close the claw fingers around game objects for gripping lifting stacking or manipulating. Attaches to structural metal via shafts and standoffs.
Appearance Description: Green plastic claw finger pieces mounted on a metal structural frame. Multiple articulated green plastic fingers. Metal crossbar or bracket forms the backbone. Overall appearance resembles a mechanical claw or gripper. Green plastic on metal structure.

Location: Metal Room, Bottom Shelf 1, Row 3, Section 3
Usage Description (What does it do): VEX claw mechanism functioning as an end-effector on robot arms. Driven by a motor and axle to open and close the claw fingers around game objects for gripping lifting stacking or manipulating. Attaches to structural metal via shafts and standoffs.
Appearance Description: Green plastic claw finger pieces mounted on a metal structural frame. Multiple articulated green plastic fingers. Metal crossbar or bracket forms the backbone. Overall appearance resembles a mechanical claw or gripper. Green plastic on metal structure.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 1, Bin 1
Usage Description (What does it do): Small spherical balls used as game objects counterweights projectiles or testing objects in robot challenges and experiments. Available in three material types: glass wood and metal steel. Each material provides different mass and surface properties.
Appearance Description: Small spherical balls approximately 16mm diameter. Three distinct types: clear transparent glass marbles and small brown wooden spheres and silver chrome metallic steel ball bearings. All small and round but vary greatly in weight and translucency.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 1, Bin 2
Usage Description (What does it do): Lightweight hollow plastic spherical balls used as game objects or for testing intake scoring and launching mechanisms on robots. Standard 40mm diameter table tennis balls. Also called table tennis balls.
Appearance Description: Small hollow round plastic balls 40mm in diameter. Smooth matte surface. Colors are white and orange. Very lightweight at approximately 2.7 grams each. Uniform perfect sphere shape.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 2, Bin 1
Usage Description (What does it do): Standard disposable plastic cups used for organizing small parts storing fasteners or as building and stacking challenge objects in robotics engineering activities.
Appearance Description: Cylindrical tapered plastic cup wider at the top than the bottom. Translucent or white plastic. Smooth interior and exterior. Standard disposable party cup size and shape.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 2, Bin 2
Usage Description (What does it do): Technical drawing tool used to draw precise circles or arcs of a specific diameter on paper. Set the radius by adjusting the leg spread then rotate around the pivot point. Used in engineering design and technical drawing tasks.
Appearance Description: Two-legged hinged metal drafting instrument. One leg ends in a sharp metal point anchor. The other leg holds a pencil or pen. Opens and closes at a central hinge to set the desired radius. Labeled compass on the body.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 2, Bin 3
Usage Description (What does it do): Precision sliding measuring instrument capable of measuring outer diameter inner diameter depth and step distances to 0.1mm or better resolution. Essential for measuring axle diameters hole sizes and part thickness in engineering design. Also called vernier caliper or digital caliper.
Appearance Description: T-shaped metallic measuring tool with two sets of jaws. Large outer jaws for measuring external dimensions. Small upper inner jaws for internal bore measurements. Thin depth probe rod extending from the far end. Sliding jaw with vernier scale markings along the main fixed beam. Silver metallic body with black measurement markings.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 3, Bin 1
Usage Description (What does it do): Standard hand cutting tool for cutting paper plastic film zip ties tape string foam and other thin materials during robot construction or design activities.
Appearance Description: Two crossing metal blades joined at a central pivot screw. Blade edges are sharpened silver metal. Loop handles are colored plastic. Standard school or office scissors size.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 3, Bin 2
Usage Description (What does it do): Solid PVA-based glue in a twist-up cylindrical applicator. Applies adhesive to paper or lightweight materials. Dries clear and flexible. Used in design documentation poster making or lightweight craft applications.
Appearance Description: Cylindrical plastic tube with a twist mechanism at the base and a cap on one end. Removing cap reveals a solid white or slightly yellow glue cylinder. Approximately the size of a large marker.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 4, Bin 1
Usage Description (What does it do): Wax or oil-based pigmented marking tools used to apply color to paper. Used for diagrams design sketches color-coded labeling and art projects in engineering and design classes.
Appearance Description: Thin round wooden cylindrical pencils with pigmented colored cores available in many vibrant colors including red blue green yellow orange and purple. Painted wooden exterior matches the core color. Standard pencil size and shape.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 4, Bin 2
Usage Description (What does it do): Straight-edged rigid measuring tool for measuring distances up to 12 inches or 30 centimeters and for drawing straight lines. Maximum measurement of 12 inches. Standard measuring and drafting tool.
Appearance Description: Long flat rigid strip of wood or clear plastic approximately 12 inches long and 1 inch wide. Thin flat profile. Measurement markings in inches on one edge and centimeters on the other. Natural wood color or transparent.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 4, Bin 3
Usage Description (What does it do): Flat wooden craft sticks used for small-scale prototype building testing structural concepts and creative engineering challenge activities.
Appearance Description: Long flat rectangular strips of light natural-colored birch wood. Smooth sanded surface. Slightly rounded ends. Standard popsicle craft stick dimensions approximately 11cm long by 1cm wide by 2mm thick.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 5, Bin 1
Usage Description (What does it do): Retractable spring-loaded measuring tape for measuring distances beyond the 12-inch limit of a ruler. Essential for measuring robot overall dimensions field element spacing and long distances in competition environments. Metal hook tab anchors the end of the tape.
Appearance Description: Compact cylindrical or rectangular plastic housing usually yellow or orange. Spring-loaded retractable flexible metal tape with measurement markings in inches and centimeters. Metal hook tab at the tape end. Lock button on housing holds tape at desired extended length.

Location: Metal Room, Supply Shelf, Row 5, Bin 2
Usage Description (What does it do): High-viscosity high-tack PVA-based craft adhesive with strong initial grab. Bonds paper fabric foam cardboard and lightweight materials. Dries flexible and clear. Stronger hold than standard glue sticks. Used in design prototyping and documentation.
Appearance Description: Soft squeezable plastic bottle with a pointed nozzle tip applicator. White opaque glue inside that dries clear. Labeled Tacky Glue or similar craft adhesive branding on the bottle.

Usage Description (What does it do): VEX tank tread links that chain together around compatible sprockets to create continuous track drive systems similar to tank treads. Also used as conveyor belts for transporting game objects. Individual links connect through pin joints. Compatible with standard VEX sprocket sizes. Also called tank treads tread links or conveyor belt links.
Appearance Description: Long flat chain of interconnected black or gray plastic rectangular links. Each link has holes on each side that engage with sprocket teeth. When assembled into a loop the chain resembles miniature tank tread or a wide flat bicycle chain.

Usage Description (What does it do): Passive low-friction roller assemblies providing rolling contact points to reduce friction guide mechanisms along surfaces or act as anti-tip devices. Each set contains four small freely-spinning wheels on a mounting bracket.
Appearance Description: Small compact black plastic central mounting bracket with four small gray or silver freely-spinning cylindrical roller wheels attached symmetrically at the corners. Resembles a miniature furniture caster assembly.

Usage Description (What does it do): The smallest size of VEX wheel that fits on standard 1/8 inch and 1/4 inch square axles. Used where space is limited as idler wheels or in lightweight low-load mechanisms. Also called VEX small wheels or mini wheels.
Appearance Description: Small diameter circular wheels with a gray or green plastic spoked hub. Rubber or foam tread on the outer rim. Significantly smaller diameter than medium or large VEX wheels. Same spoke-and-hub construction as larger wheels but much smaller.

Usage Description (What does it do): Mid-size VEX wheels used in drive trains requiring a balance between speed and torque. Fits both 1/8 inch and 1/4 inch square axles with appropriate inserts. Common choice for competition drive trains. Also called VEX medium traction wheels.
Appearance Description: Medium diameter circular wheels with a green plastic spoked hub and rubber or foam tread pattern on the outer circumference. Green spokes radiate from center hub to outer rim. Larger than small wheels and smaller than large wheels.

Usage Description (What does it do): Small 1 to 2 pound free weights used to add ballast or counterweight mass to a robot. Lowers center of gravity increases drive traction through added downforce or counterbalances a heavy arm or mechanism.
Appearance Description: Classic dumbbell shape with two large hexagonal weight plate heads on either end of a short cylindrical handle bar. Black iron or dark metallic gray finish. Much heavier and denser than any plastic VEX component despite small size.

Usage Description (What does it do): Heavy-duty 15-tooth sprocket designed for high-torque VEX chain and tread drive systems. Thicker body than standard sprockets distributes load across more material reducing stress fracture risk. Compatible with high-strength chain links and VEX treads. Capable of supporting heavy lift loads.
Appearance Description: Thick wide-body plastic sprocket with exactly 15 large evenly-spaced teeth around the circumference. Noticeably thicker and more robust cross-section than standard-thickness sprockets. Square center hub for axle attachment with screw holes for metal shaft inserts.

Usage Description (What does it do): Large spur gear with 60 teeth used in gear train mechanisms to create large speed reductions or torque multiplications. Paired with a 12-tooth pinion creates a 5:1 reduction. Has additional mounting holes across the face for use as a turntable or rotating platform base. Meshes with all standard VEX spur gears.
Appearance Description: Large thin circular red plastic gear. 60 small evenly-spaced teeth around the outer circumference. Several additional mounting holes through the gear face. Large square center hole for axle. Red color distinguishes it from smaller gears.

Usage Description (What does it do): The largest standard VEX spur gear with 84 teeth providing the highest single-stage reduction available at 7:1 when paired with a 12-tooth pinion. Mounting holes across the face allow use as a turntable base or rotating platform. Meshes with all VEX spur gears.
Appearance Description: Very large thin circular plastic gear with 84 small evenly-spaced teeth around the outer circumference. Largest gear diameter in the standard VEX lineup. Multiple mounting holes distributed across the gear face. Red or gray plastic. Much larger diameter than 60-tooth gear.

Usage Description (What does it do): Large 30-tooth sprocket for VEX chain and tread systems providing significant torque multiplication when paired with smaller drive sprockets. Used in lifting mechanisms and high-load drive systems requiring torque amplification.
Appearance Description: Large circular plastic sprocket with 30 large rounded teeth evenly spaced around the circumference. Square center hole for axle insertion. Screw holes in the body for metal shaft inserts. Larger diameter than 18 and 24 tooth sprockets.

Usage Description (What does it do): Medium-large 24-tooth sprocket for VEX chain and tread systems offering a good balance of speed and torque for drive train ratios. Creates 2:1 reduction with a 12-tooth sprocket.
Appearance Description: Circular plastic sprocket with 24 large evenly-spaced teeth. Square center hole for axle insertion. Screw holes in the body. Medium-large diameter between 18 and 30 tooth sprockets.

Usage Description (What does it do): The smallest standard VEX spur gear also called a pinion gear. Used most commonly as the motor output gear in gear train reductions. Paired with a 60-tooth gear creates a 5:1 torque multiplication. Meshes with all standard VEX spur gears.
Appearance Description: Smallest VEX spur gear. Small thin circular plastic gear with 12 small teeth and the smallest gear diameter. Square center hole. Typically black or dark gray plastic. Much smaller than all other gears.

Usage Description (What does it do): A linear gear rack that meshes with a VEX spur gear to convert continuous rotary motor motion into linear back-and-forth sliding motion. Mounts to VEX metal structure using screws through holes along its body. Used in linear actuators scissor lifts and linear slide drives. Also called gear rack or linear rack.
Appearance Description: Flat elongated rectangular red plastic strip with teeth running along one long edge. Mounting holes along the body for attaching to VEX metal structure. Flat rectangular profile. Red color distinguishes from green rack.

Usage Description (What does it do): Identical function to the red rack: a linear gear rack that converts rotary gear motion into linear sliding motion. Meshes with standard VEX spur gears. Same mounting and meshing specifications as the red rack. Color is the only visual distinction between the two rack types.
Appearance Description: Flat elongated green plastic strip with teeth running along one long edge. Mounting holes along the body. Flat rectangular profile. Green color distinguishes it from the red rack.

Usage Description (What does it do): A threaded rod mechanism that converts rotary motor input into precise controlled linear motion via a matching threaded nut or bushing. Offers very high mechanical advantage and is inherently self-locking meaning it holds position when the motor stops. Used for slow precise linear lifts clamping mechanisms and fine positioning systems.
Appearance Description: Long thick rod with deep coarse helical screw threads running the full length. Much larger thread pitch than a standard screw. Threads are deep and coarse. Much thicker and longer than a worm screw.

Usage Description (What does it do): A grooved wheel used to redirect and transmit tension forces via string rope or elastic cord. Can be used in block-and-tackle pulley systems to create mechanical advantage for lifting or to redirect cord to change the direction of an actuator force. Also called a sheave or cord pulley.
Appearance Description: Small circular wheel with a distinct V-shaped or U-shaped groove cut around the outer circumference to guide and retain string or cord. Square or round center hole for axle mounting. Plastic construction in green or gray.

Usage Description (What does it do): A helical single-thread screw gear that meshes perpendicularly with a standard spur gear to achieve very high torque multiplication in a compact form typically 12:1 per stage while rotating the output axis by 90 degrees. Worm drive systems are self-locking so the gear cannot back-drive the worm. Ideal for lifts winches and precision positioning. Also called worm gear or worm drive.
Appearance Description: Small compact cylindrical part with a spiraling single helical thread wrapping around it like a corkscrew. Fits on an axle through a square center hole. Much shorter than a lead screw. Silver metallic or dark plastic finish.

Usage Description (What does it do): A gear with teeth cut at an angle on a conical face to transfer rotary motion between two shafts at 90 degrees to each other. Used in pairs to redirect the axis of rotation. Common in steering systems differential builds and anywhere motion must turn a corner. Also called mitre gear or conical gear.
Appearance Description: Conical tapered gear shape with teeth angled diagonally across the sloped face rather than straight as on spur gears. Square center hole for axle insertion. Gray or black plastic. The angled conical tooth face is the key visual identifier.

Usage Description (What does it do): A mechanical gearbox assembly containing internal bevel gears that splits torque from a single input between two output shafts while allowing each output to spin at a different speed. Used in drivetrain applications so wheels turn at different rates during cornering or in advanced mechanisms requiring two independently controlled outputs from one motor. Also called gear differential or bevel differential.
Appearance Description: A rectangular plastic box housing enclosing an internal bevel gear assembly. Two output shafts protrude from opposite sides of the housing. The outer housing can itself be driven or held fixed to control behavior. Black or gray plastic casing. Box-like shape with axle stubs on two opposing sides.

Usage Description (What does it do): Individual chain links that connect together to form a continuous drive chain looped around two or more sprockets to transfer rotational power over distance. Each link engages the sprocket teeth as it passes over them. Compatible with standard VEX sprockets. Also called VEX chain or roller chain links.
Appearance Description: Small individual black or gray plastic links each with two holes on opposing sides that engage with sprocket teeth. When multiple links are joined in series they form a chain loop resembling a miniature bicycle chain.

Usage Description (What does it do): The outer channel piece of a VEX linear slide mechanism. The inner slide fits inside this outer track and travels smoothly along its length creating a telescoping linear extension system. Mounted to the robot frame. Used in arm extensions linear lifts or any mechanism requiring straight-line travel. Also called slide track or linear slide channel.
Appearance Description: Small rectangular plastic channel or track with smooth inner walls. Open along one face to accept the inner slide piece. Has mounting holes for attaching to the robot structure. Slightly larger profile than the inner slide it houses.

Usage Description (What does it do): The sliding inner component of a VEX linear slide mechanism that moves along the inside of the outer slide channel with very low friction. Enables smooth telescoping linear extension when actuated. Also called slide insert or linear slide bar.
Appearance Description: Small smooth flat plastic rectangular piece sized to slide inside the outer slide channel with minimal clearance. Smooth on all surfaces. Slightly smaller profile than the outer slide it fits within.

Usage Description (What does it do): Medium-sized 18-tooth sprocket for VEX chain and tread systems. Creates a 1:1 drive ratio when paired with another 18-tooth sprocket. A common general-purpose sprocket size for balanced drive applications.
Appearance Description: Circular plastic sprocket with 18 large evenly-spaced teeth around the circumference. Square center hole for axle insertion. Screw holes in the body. Medium diameter between 12 and 24 tooth sprockets.

Usage Description (What does it do): An eccentric rotating cam with an Archimedean spiral profile resembling a snail shell. As it rotates it pushes a cam follower outward in a smooth controlled non-uniform linear motion before releasing. Used to create periodic pushing indexing or punching mechanisms. Part of a cam-and-follower system converting continuous rotation into controlled reciprocating linear motion.
Appearance Description: Asymmetric plastic part with a spiral snail-shell or conch-shell shaped profile. Square center hole for axle insertion. One edge is a continuous smooth spiral curve that increases in radius from one end to the other. Green or black plastic.

Usage Description (What does it do): Spoked roller wheels with high-friction flexible projections on their outer surface used to actively draw in and funnel game objects through an intake mechanism. The flexible spokes grip objects and pull them inward when powered by a motor. Common in VEX competition robot intake and indexer systems.
Appearance Description: Wheel with radially projecting flexible rubber spokes or bump projections on the outer surface creating a star or asterisk cross-section. Hub is green or black plastic. Rubber or soft plastic flexible spokes provide grip and distinguish from standard wheels.

Usage Description (What does it do): The smallest standard VEX sprocket with 12 teeth. Used as high-speed low-torque motor output sprockets for maximum speed drive ratios. Creates a 1:2 speed increase when paired with a 24-tooth sprocket. Compatible with VEX chain links.
Appearance Description: Smallest VEX sprocket. Small circular plastic piece with 12 large teeth relative to the small body size. Square center hole for axle insertion. Smallest sprocket diameter in the standard lineup.

Usage Description (What does it do): A cylindrical spool that wraps string cord or cable around itself as a motor drives it converting rotary motor motion into linear pulling or lifting force via the string. End plates (flanges) contain the wrapped string and prevent it from slipping off the spool. Used in string-based winch lifts and launching mechanisms.
Appearance Description: Short central cylindrical spool body flanked by two large flat circular end plates (flanges) that contain the cord. Overall shape resembles a thread bobbin yo-yo or cable drum. Fits on an axle through a square center hole. Plastic construction.

Usage Description (What does it do): An L-shaped hand crank attachment for an axle that allows manual rotation of any mechanism by hand without motor power. Used for demonstration manual override testing mechanism ranges or as a human-powered input device.
Appearance Description: L-shaped plastic lever with a right-angle bend. One end has a square hole for axle insertion. The other end serves as the hand grip. The L shape provides leverage for manual rotation. Plastic construction.

Usage Description (What does it do): The driven output component in a cam-and-follower mechanism. Pressed against the rotating cam surface and as the cam rotates its profile pushes the follower outward in a controlled pattern converting rotation into reciprocating linear motion. A small wheel on the follower tip reduces friction against the cam surface. Paired with the snail cam or similar cam.
Appearance Description: A small green plastic column or post with a tiny freely-spinning wheel at the contact end that rides against the cam surface. The column slides linearly while the wheel rolls against the cam. Small and lightweight.

Usage Description (What does it do): Medium-large VEX spur gear with 36 teeth. Creates a 3:1 torque multiplication when driven by a 12-tooth pinion. Commonly used in arm mechanisms and drive trains. Meshes with all standard VEX spur gears.
Appearance Description: Medium-large thin circular plastic gear with 36 evenly-spaced teeth around the outer circumference. Square center hole for axle. Diameter between 24-tooth and 60-tooth gears. Red or gray plastic.

Usage Description (What does it do): Medium-large 24-tooth sprocket for VEX chain and tread systems. Common size for balanced drive train sprocket ratios. Creates a 2:1 reduction with a 12-tooth sprocket.
Appearance Description: Circular plastic sprocket with 24 large evenly-spaced teeth. Square center hole for axle insertion. Screw holes in the body for metal shaft inserts.

Usage Description (What does it do): Medium VEX spur gear with 24 teeth. Creates a 2:1 reduction when driven by a 12-tooth pinion. Used in many gear train configurations requiring moderate speed reduction. Meshes with all standard VEX spur gears.
Appearance Description: Medium circular thin plastic gear with 24 evenly-spaced small teeth around the circumference. Square center hole for axle. Diameter between 12-tooth and 36-tooth gears. Typically black or dark gray plastic.

Usage Description (What does it do): The smallest VEX sprocket with only 6 teeth. Used on motor output shafts for maximum chain drive speed with minimum torque. Creates the fastest possible sprocket ratio in a chain drive system. Compatible with VEX chain links.
Appearance Description: Very small circular plastic sprocket with only 6 large teeth. Square center hole. Smallest sprocket diameter in the VEX lineup. Teeth appear large relative to the very small body size.

Usage Description (What does it do): A one-way ratcheting gear that allows free rotation in one direction but prevents reverse rotation when a pawl or sprawl engages its asymmetric teeth. Used to hold a load prevent back-driving a lift or create a one-way mechanical drive. Also called ratchet gear or ratchet wheel.
Appearance Description: Circular plastic disc with asymmetric sawtooth teeth around the outer circumference. Each tooth has one gradual slope for sliding over the pawl and one sharp vertical face to catch and block reverse rotation. Similar in size to a spur gear but tooth profile is distinctly asymmetric and non-uniform.

Usage Description (What does it do): A metal clamping ring that slides onto an axle and is secured with a set screw to prevent parts from sliding axially along the shaft. Placed on either side of a gear wheel or sprocket to fix its position on the axle. Also called axle collar set collar or shaft clamp.
Appearance Description: Small circular metal ring with a 1/8 inch square center hole for the axle and a perpendicular screw hole for the set screw. Flat short cylindrical shape. Silver metallic finish. Set screw head visible on the outer cylindrical surface.

Usage Description (What does it do): A flat metal structural bracket in a plus or cross shape used to join multiple VEX metal bars simultaneously at their intersection. Creates a strong central junction connecting up to four bars in perpendicular directions. Made from 0.046 inch thick zinc-plated cold rolled steel.
Appearance Description: Flat thin metal plate in a symmetrical plus sign or cross shape. Four equal arms extending from a central point. Screw holes at the tip of each arm and at the center. Silver zinc-plated steel surface.

Usage Description (What does it do): A flat metal bracket bent at 45 degrees used to connect VEX structural bars at 45-degree angles. Provides diagonal bracing or constructs angled frame sections. Made from 0.046 inch thick zinc-plated cold rolled steel.
Appearance Description: Flat thin metal plate with a 45-degree angle bend. Screw holes on each flat section for attachment to structural metal. Silver zinc-plated steel. The bend angle is visibly less than a right angle and more than a straight line.

Usage Description (What does it do): A flat metal L-shaped bracket for rigidly connecting two VEX structural metal bars at 90-degree right angles. The most common corner connector in VEX robot frame construction. Made from 0.046 inch thick zinc-plated cold rolled steel. Also called L-bracket or corner gusset.
Appearance Description: Flat thin metal plate with a 90-degree right-angle bend giving it an L shape. Screw holes on each arm for attachment. Silver zinc-plated steel finish. Both arms approximately equal in length.

Usage Description (What does it do): A flat metal quarter-circle shaped bracket used to support angled connections in VEX robot structures or as a pivot point. Made from 0.046 inch thick zinc-plated cold rolled steel.
Appearance Description: Flat thin metal plate in a quarter-circle fan or pie-slice shape. Two straight edges meeting at a right angle with a curved arc edge connecting them. Screw holes along both straight edges. Silver zinc-plated steel.

Usage Description (What does it do): Very thin flat circular metal discs with a center hole used as axle spacers load distributors under screw heads friction reducers between moving parts or for fine spacing adjustments between components. Thinner than any plastic spacer. Also called flat washers.
Appearance Description: Very thin small flat circular metal disc with a center hole. Almost no measurable thickness compared to a spacer. Silver metallic finish. Much thinner and more flexible than any plastic spacer.

Usage Description (What does it do): A hexagonal #8-32 nut with an integrated serrated lock washer flange on one face. Can be hand-tightened onto screws making assembly fast. The serrated flange provides light vibration resistance but loosens more easily than nylock nuts. Used for lighter-duty attachments or frequent disassembly. Also called kep nut k-lock nut or external tooth lock nut.
Appearance Description: Small hexagonal metal nut with a built-in serrated or toothed washer flange on one face. Silver metallic. The washer flange makes it slightly larger in diameter than a plain hex nut. Thinner overall profile than a nylock nut.

Usage Description (What does it do): A nylon-insert locking hex nut for #8-32 screws. The nylon insert in the top portion deforms around the screw threads creating strong vibration-resistant locking. Requires a tool to install but provides superior holding strength. Preferred fastener for all high-stress structural connections in VEX robots. Also called nylock nyloc or nylon insert lock nut.
Appearance Description: Hexagonal metal nut that is thicker than a standard nut. One end has a distinctive raised cylindrical nylon plastic collar visibly protruding above the metal hex body. Nylon collar is white or off-white. Silver metallic hex body below the nylon.

Usage Description (What does it do): Assortment of #8-32 socket-head cap screws in various lengths including 1/4 inch 1/2 inch 3/4 inch and 1 inch. The universal primary fastener for all VEX structural assembly. Used with keps nuts or nylock nuts to bolt all metal and plastic components together. Also called VEX screws socket head screws or Allen head screws.
Appearance Description: Black anodized metal screws with a smooth cylindrical head and hexagonal socket Allen key recess on the top face. Threaded shaft with #8-32 thread pitch. Various shaft lengths mixed in the same bin. Head diameter is consistent across all lengths.

Usage Description (What does it do): Assortment of #8-32 socket-head cap screws in various lengths including 1/4 inch 1/2 inch 3/4 inch and 1 inch. The universal primary fastener for all VEX structural assembly. Used with keps nuts or nylock nuts to bolt all metal and plastic components together. Also called VEX screws socket head screws or Allen head screws.
Appearance Description: Black anodized metal screws with a smooth cylindrical head and hexagonal socket Allen key recess on the top face. Threaded shaft with #8-32 thread pitch. Various shaft lengths mixed in the same bin. Head diameter is consistent across all lengths.

Usage Description (What does it do): A short smooth plastic cylinder with a square center hole that slides onto an axle to create precise spacing between parts. Used to separate gears from walls fill shaft gaps or position components at specific distances. Available in multiple lengths. Also called axle spacer or nylon spacer.
Appearance Description: Short black plastic cylinder with a square center hole running through its full length. Smooth outer cylindrical surface. Larger and notably thicker than a washer. Resembles a miniature plastic barrel or bushing.

Usage Description (What does it do): A plastic clip that snaps into the square holes of VEX metal structure and holds a nylock nut in alignment allowing a screw to be tightened one-handed without separately gripping the nut. Increases structural integrity by adding additional surface contact. Also called nut retainer nut clip or nut holder.
Appearance Description: Small black or dark gray plastic piece with a hexagonal cavity that captures and holds a nylock nut. Designed to snap into the square holes of VEX structural metal. Small and lightweight.

Part Name: Hex Nut Retainer with Bearing Flat
Usage Description (What does it do): A combined plastic part that provides nut retention for one-handed assembly and also includes an extended bearing hub through which an axle can pass. Provides both fastening convenience and low-friction axle support in a single part.
Appearance Description: Similar to the standard hex nut retainer but with an extended cylindrical bearing hub protruding from one face. The bearing hub has a square center hole for axle passage. Black or dark gray plastic. Larger and taller than the standard nut retainer due to the extended bearing hub.

Usage Description (What does it do): A threaded hexagonal metal cylinder used to create a precise fixed 1 inch spacing between two parallel structural plates. Both ends are internally threaded to accept #8-32 screws. Used to build double-layer frames offset electronics boards or create enclosed structural assemblies. Also called 1 inch hex standoff or 1 inch spacer post.
Appearance Description: Hexagonal cross-section metal cylinder with flat ends and internally threaded holes on both ends. Silver metallic finish. Exactly 1 inch long. Same hex diameter as all other standoffs. Longer than the 0.5 inch standoff.

Usage Description (What does it do): A threaded hexagonal metal cylinder used to create a precise fixed 0.5 inch spacing between two structural plates. Both ends internally threaded for #8-32 screws. The shortest available standoff. Also called half inch hex standoff.
Appearance Description: Hexagonal cross-section metal cylinder. Silver metallic. Shortest of all standoffs at only 0.5 inches long. Same hex diameter as all other standoffs. Both flat ends have internally threaded holes.

Usage Description (What does it do): A threaded hexagonal metal cylinder creating a 3 inch fixed spacing between structural plates. Both ends threaded for #8-32 screws. The longest available standoff used for wide frame offsets or mounting components far from the main structure. Also called 3 inch hex standoff.
Appearance Description: Hexagonal cross-section metal cylinder. Silver metallic. Longest standoff at 3 inches. Same hex diameter as shorter standoffs but noticeably longer. Both flat ends have internally threaded holes.

Usage Description (What does it do): A threaded hexagonal metal cylinder creating a 2 inch fixed spacing between structural plates. Both ends threaded for #8-32 screws. Medium-long standoff for moderate frame offsets. Also called 2 inch hex standoff.
Appearance Description: Hexagonal cross-section metal cylinder. Silver metallic. 2 inches long. Same hex diameter as other standoffs. Length is between 1 inch and 3 inch standoffs.

Usage Description (What does it do): A plastic plate that is mounted on VEX metal so that an axle or shaft passes through it instead of passing directly through the metal hole. The shaft goes through the bearing flat before it would otherwise come into contact with the metal plate. This prevents the rotating shaft from directly touching or wearing the metal hole. Provides low-friction plastic surface for the shaft to spin against rather than grinding against metal. Best practice is to place a bearing flat on every metal surface that a rotating shaft passes through. Also called bearing block or axle bearing plate.
Appearance Description: Flat rectangular black plastic plate with three holes in a line: two outer holes for screws or snap rivets and one center hole that serves as the bearing surface for the axle. Slightly raised bearing collar surrounds the center hole. Smooth black finish.

Usage Description (What does it do): A bearing housing that supports a rotating axle running parallel to the mounting surface and elevated above it. Attached to the robot frame via screws. Used when a shaft needs support above and away from the structural plate such as in cantilevered wheel setups or elevated drive shafts. Also called pillow block or flange bearing.
Appearance Description: Black plastic housing block with a shaft hole running parallel to (not perpendicular to) its flat mounting base. Two screw holes on the flat base for mounting. The bearing housing protrudes above the mounting surface. Looks like a small rectangular block with a hole through its side.

Usage Description (What does it do): A small metal insert pressed into the center hub of gears sprockets or wheels to provide a secure strong interface with the axle. The square hole forces the part to rotate with the axle rather than spinning freely on it. Preferred over plastic inserts in high-torque applications. Also called metal gear insert or metal axle insert.
Appearance Description: Small square or round metal piece that press-fits into the center hole of a VEX gear or sprocket. Square hole through the center for the axle. Silver metallic finish. Very small component.

Usage Description (What does it do): A thin bar that inserts into a slot in a VEX gear or sprocket to lock it rotationally to the axle preventing free spinning. Forces the part to turn with the axle. An alternative to the metal shaft insert for specific part designs that use slots instead of inserts.
Appearance Description: Thin flat black bar with a square hole. Inserts into slots on the side of VEX gears or sprockets to lock rotation to the axle. Long thin flat profile. Square hole is the key feature for axle engagement.

Usage Description (What does it do): Square cross-section steel axles 4 inches long used as rotating shafts for wheels gears sprockets and motor connections in VEX mechanisms. Square profile locks parts with square holes in rotational alignment. Also called 4 inch shaft or VEX axle.
Appearance Description: Straight metal rod with a small square cross-section. Silver or steel gray color. 4 inches long. Smooth surface. Square profile visible when viewed end-on.

Usage Description (What does it do): Square cross-section steel axles 3 inches long for rotating shaft applications in VEX mechanisms. Common medium-length axle for wheel and gear assemblies. Also called 3 inch shaft or VEX axle.
Appearance Description: Straight metal rod with a small square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. 3 inches long. Smooth surface. Shorter than the 4 inch axle.

Usage Description (What does it do): Square cross-section steel axles 2 inches long for short rotating shaft applications. The shortest standard labeled axle length. Also called 2 inch shaft or short axle.
Appearance Description: Straight metal rod with a small square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. 2 inches long. Smooth surface. Short compared to 3 and 4 inch axles.

Usage Description (What does it do): Square cross-section steel axles shorter than 2 inches used for very compact rotating shaft applications in tight spaces. The shortest available VEX axle category. Also called short axle or stub axle.
Appearance Description: Straight metal rod with a small square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. Less than 2 inches long. Very short stub axle.

Usage Description (What does it do): A connector piece that joins two separate VEX axles end-to-end to create a single longer combined shaft for applications requiring length beyond what a single axle provides. Has a square hole running through its full length to accept axles from both ends. Also called axle coupler or shaft extender.
Appearance Description: Short black shiny plastic or metal cylindrical or rectangular tube. Square hole runs through the full length. Slightly thicker in outer diameter than the axle itself. Both ends accept square axles. Smooth exterior surface.

Usage Description (What does it do): The longest available #8-32 socket-head cap screw for VEX construction. Used when joining very thick multi-layer assemblies attaching standoffs through stacked structure or wherever extra thread engagement depth is required. Same thread pitch as all other VEX screws.
Appearance Description: Black anodized metal screw. Identical cylindrical socket head with hexagonal Allen key recess as other VEX screws but with a noticeably longer threaded shaft than all other screws in the assortment.

Usage Description (What does it do): A plastic insert that goes into the center hub of a gear or sprocket to allow the axle to spin freely through the part. The circular hole means the gear rotates on the axle rather than with it. Used for idler gears and idler sprockets. Opposite function from the metal shaft insert. Also called plastic gear insert or idler insert.
Appearance Description: Small round plastic piece with a circular (not square) center hole. Gray and green two-tone plastic. Fits into VEX gear and sprocket center holes. The circular hole distinguishes it from the metal insert which has a square hole.

Usage Description (What does it do): Snap-in plastic push rivets for quickly attaching bearing flats pillow blocks or other plastic bearing parts to VEX metal structure without screws. Snap into the square holes in VEX metal and lock in place. Reusable and convenient but less rigid than screw attachment. Also called snap rivets push rivets or bearing rivets.
Appearance Description: Small black plastic two-piece rivet. Outer body and an inner pin. When the inner pin is pushed in it expands the back of the rivet to lock it in the metal square hole. Small cylindrical body sized to fit VEX metal square holes.

Usage Description (What does it do): A rubber elastomer ring that grips an axle through friction without requiring a set screw or tool. Quick no-tool alternative to metal shaft collars for light-duty applications. Not fully secure under high load as it can slip. Also called rubber collar or friction collar.
Appearance Description: Flexible rubbery soft plastic ring with a circular center hole sized to grip the axle surface. Cylindrical ring shape. Soft and deformable. Very different feel and texture from the rigid metal shaft collar.

Usage Description (What does it do): A 12-inch VEX square steel axle in excellent straight condition with no deformation. The longest axle available. Functions as a rotating shaft for wheels gears and sprockets across long spans. Preferred for applications requiring precise alignment over long distances. Also called 12 inch shaft or long axle. This specific axle is in very straight undamaged condition.
Appearance Description: Long straight metal rod with square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. 12 inches long. No visible bends curves or deformations whatsoever. Perfectly straight from end to end when viewed from any angle or placed flat on a surface.

Usage Description (What does it do): A 12-inch VEX square steel axle that has sustained minor deformation from prior use. Same type and function as the standard 12-inch axle but this specific axle has a slight bow along its length. Still usable for lower-precision or lower-speed applications. May introduce slight vibration at high RPM. This axle is slightly bent.
Appearance Description: Long metal rod with square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. 12 inches long. Has a slight visible bow or gentle curve along its length. The deviation from straight is noticeable when viewed from the end or when rolled on a flat surface but not extreme.

Usage Description (What does it do): A 12-inch VEX square steel axle that has been severely deformed through extreme stress or misuse. Same part type as the standard 12-inch axle but this specific axle is significantly bent. Not recommended for active mechanisms as it causes severe vibration. Should be replaced. This axle is very bent.
Appearance Description: Long metal rod with square cross-section. Silver steel gray color. 12 inches long. Visibly and severely bent or kinked along its length. Clearly and obviously not straight when compared to a flat surface.
